newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka blasts rebel claim that food stopped.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka blasts rebel claim that food stopped.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Monday blasted a Tamil Tiger separatists' claim that food supplies to the rebel heartland had been stopped, saying it was an attempt by the guerrillas to divert attention from recent battlefield reversals.

"The government of Sri Lanka wishes to categorically state that there has been no change in the government's long followed policy of sending all essential supplies required by the people in the uncleared areas," a Foreign Ministry statement said.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) said at the weekend that no food convoys had been sent to the northern Wanni region for four days on instructions by the Sri Lankan military.
The ministry statement said 261 trucks, each carrying 10 tonnes of essential supplies, had been sent to the Wanni in 10 days to June 9.
The statement said that it had not been possible to send food into the rebel heartland since then as lorries had not returned to the loading point from the Wanni.
LTTE spokesmen in London were not immediately available for comment on Monday.
The ministry statement said the rebels were trying to divert attention from the reversals they were facing in the on-going Operation "Jaya Sikuru" (Sure of Victory).
The military launched the operation last month to open a crucial highway linking the government-held town of Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Vavuniya lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
The rebels struck back last week when they launched a daring attack at the army's rear, breaching military defences just north of Vavuniya and killing more than 100 troops.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, have accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying crops and property under the pretext of opening a supply route, and of continuing a food siege of the Wanni.

The ministry statement said that Sri Lanka had not used food as a weapon in the war against the separatists and had continued to supply essential items to the rebel-held areas inspite of the knowledge that "a bulk of these supplies are comandeered by the LTTE for their sustenance".

The military said earlier this month that it had recovered huge stockpiles of food in Nedunkeni, apparently left behind by the LTTE when the government troops captured the northeastern town after fierce fighting.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as international media have not been allowed in the war zone.
